inputs.share_count_basis: 2,713,665,096 shares issued at 31-Mar-2026 (FY26 AR share-capital note), which includes ~4.75m treasury shares held by the ESOP trust for employee awards; weighted diluted count was 2,712.3m. Issued count used as the conservative fully diluted figure. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; the trust's treasury-share purchases are the cash mechanism that keeps it flat.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 AR consolidated cash flow 'Share based payment to employees' 478 crore (Annual_FY2026.txt:21985). No net-share-settlement tax line; awards are settled from ESOP-trust treasury shares (711 crore bought FY26), whose cost the expense already captures.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T09:59:15Z (NSE, 15:29 IST, last minute of the Friday session; Yahoo chart API)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR, the flows' own currency: India 10y G-Sec ~6.5% + beta ~0.9 x India ERP ~6.0% = cost of equity ~11.9%; the group has effectively no debt (borrowings 159 crore), so WACC = CoE, rounded to 12.0%. Terminal growth 5% INR nominal = ~2-3% USD growth plus ~2-3% structural INR depreciation (India inflation ~4%). Same WACC in every scenario: risk is charged in the flows (25% bear weight), not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: FY26 'Payment of lease liabilities including interest' 1,685 crore (16,850m, 1.29% of revenue; Annual_FY2026.txt:22022) deducted via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (5,056 crore) EXCLUDED from net debt; da_pct is ex right-of-use depreciation (total D&A 3.35% less ~1.0% ROU) so cash-tax EBIT does not double-charge the lease.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is 32 crore of 75,197 crore equity (0.04%) - immaterial; not deducted, flows treated as attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 2: non-US operating company, IT services; adaptations read - INR WACC, lease treatment B, NCI immaterial, near-SBC-zero). No prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry: fresh build. FY0 = FY2026 (year to 31-Mar-2026). Revenue 130,144 crore; EBITDA ex the one-time New Labour Codes charge (956 crore) 26,752 crore = 20.56%; adj. EBITDA margin (pre-SBC, the engine deducts SBC separately) 20.92%. INTEREST: interest income (1,542 crore) is removed in OCF and received in investing, and EBITDA here is pre other-income, so the flows already exclude it - interest_income set to 0 to avoid deducting it twice; the treasury pile is added in the bridge. OWNER FCF FY26 = reported FCF 185,530 (OCF 199,750 - capex 14,220) - SBC 4,780 - lease payments 16,850 = 163,900m (12.6% of revenue). CASH: treasury investments per MD&A (debt MFs 3,229 + debt securities 3,731 + bank deposits 21,303 + corporate deposits 1,066 = 29,329 crore = 293,290m; Annual_FY2026.txt:6720-6726), conservatively excluding operating current-account cash; debt = borrowings 159 crore. Q2 FY27 (Sep-2026) balance sheet not extracted; March 2026 is the latest filed balance sheet in the folder - net cash likely higher by H1 FY27 retained cash, a small understatement. CAPEX path 2.0% = ~1.1% PP&E/intangibles capex + ~0.9% recurring bolt-on M&A (Jaspersoft $240M and HPE Telco $160M pending; FY25 acquisitions 1,982 crore), because the growth path includes ~0.9pp/yr inorganic contribution per FY27 guidance. WC: services receivables (billed+unbilled ~25% of revenue) less payables/contract liabilities -> wc_capture -15% of the revenue increase (FY26: receivables +2,248 crore on +13,089 crore revenue). CASH TAX 23.5%: FY26 ETR 23.6%, FY25 25.2%; cash paid ~18-19% of PBT but current tax liabilities rose 1,047 crore, so accrual-like 23.5% used. GROWTH is in INR as reported: FY27 guidance is +2.5-4.0% constant currency, but Q2 FY27 reported +11.5% INR vs +2.6% cc on rupee weakness; with H1 in hand FY27 INR revenue ~+9%. Buybacks: the only repurchases are ESOP-trust treasury purchases (711 crore FY26); capital return is ~90%+ dividend payout, so the flat count is funded.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (4.6-4.8%) diverges >30% from revenue (8.7-11.6%) and EPS 5y (8.4%): HCLTech pays out ~90-98% of net income as dividends, so book value does not compound and is not a usable growth proxy. Revenue 3y CAGR selected instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs on the SBC-adjusted series (reported FCF less SBC; lease payments not deducted historically because the pre-FY25 lease cash lines were not extracted). FY21 FCF (177,140) is inflated by a COVID-era receivables release, which flattens the 5y FCF CAGR; FY26 OCF also carried the 956 crore labour-code charge and a 2,248 crore receivables build. SBC is small (0.2-0.4% of revenue) and not growing faster than cash flow - the reported vs SBC-adjusted gap is ~0.3pp. EPS 3y CAGR depressed by the FY26 labour-code and tax items (61.36 vs 64.09 in FY25).

base.narrative: FY27 INR revenue ~+9% (cc guidance 2.5-4% plus rupee weakness and ~0.9pp inorganic); then 7-8% INR (4-5% USD) fading to 5.5% as AI deflation in legacy ADM/BPO offsets AI-led deal wins. EBIT held in the 17.5-18.5% guided band (adj. EBITDA ~21.5%).

bull.narrative: Advanced AI revenue ($876M annualized, 1.4x in two quarters) and record TCV ($9.3B FY26, $3.3B in Q2 FY27) convert into 6-7% USD growth; ERS rides semiconductor/Physical-AI R&D outsourcing; software stabilises; outcome-based pricing lifts adj. EBITDA to 23% (EBIT ~19.5%).

bear.narrative: FY27 is largely booked (H1 done), but from FY28 AI-native delivery deflates labour-based ADM/BPO/testing revenue faster than AI wins replace it; HCLSoftware keeps shrinking in cc; US/Europe discretionary spend stays soft and H-1B costs rise. USD revenue roughly flat for three years (INR +3-4% on rupee drift only) and adj. EBITDA compresses ~2.5pp to 19% (EBIT ~15.5%).

scenario_narratives.base: HCLTech keeps growing modestly ahead of TCS/Infosys in constant currency (4-5% USD) as AI-led deal wins and bolt-on M&A roughly offset AI-driven deflation in legacy application and BPO work; EBIT stays within the 17.5-18.5% guided band and near-full payout continues. INR revenue +9% in FY27 (rupee tailwind, H1 delivered) fading to 5.5% by year 10.
scenario_narratives.bull: HCLTech's early AI positioning (Advanced AI revenue $876M annualized, OpenAI/NVIDIA partnerships, AI Force across 75+ accounts) and engineering heritage capture the semiconductor/Physical-AI outsourcing wave: record bookings translate into 6-7% USD growth for five years, HCLSoftware stabilises, and outcome-based pricing lifts adj. EBITDA to 23%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The company's own flagged risk materialises: AI-native delivery and client insourcing deflate labour-arbitrage revenue faster than new AI streams scale, HCLSoftware keeps declining, US/Europe discretionary IT budgets stay weak and visa costs rise. USD revenue stalls for three years and margins compress ~2.5pp as pricing power erodes while AI-talent costs rise.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because AI-led pricing deflation is a structural threat the company itself discloses and the evidence on whether AI revenue offsets it is two quarters old. Base 50% reflects guidance raised after Q2 FY27 and a clean, net-cash balance sheet with no solvency tail. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs AI revenue scaling, software stabilising and margin expansion all at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF in INR: unlevered FCF after SBC and full lease cash, discounted at a 12% INR cost of capital, plus ~29,300 crore of treasury investments. HCLTech is a mature, cash-generative, near-SBC-free services compounder returning ~90%+ of earnings; value hinges on whether 4-5% USD growth and ~18% EBIT survive AI deflation of labour-based services.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI/GenAI deflation of labour-based ADM, BPO and testing revenue (company-flagged, high severity)
INR/USD path: INR-denominated growth assumes ~2-3% annual rupee depreciation; a stable rupee lowers INR revenue growth roughly one-for-one
HCLSoftware decline (-4.1% cc FY26) eroding the highest-margin segment
US/Europe discretionary IT-spend weakness and H-1B fee/immigration policy
Terminal value ~2/3 of EV; 12% INR WACC vs 5% terminal growth drives most of the value
